_note: US dollars per million tokens, per model, as your provider account bills them. A dated model name (gpt-x-2026-01-01) takes the price of its longest listed prefix. Fill in a model to see runs' cost in dollars (cognalys cost) and to use --max-cost; without a price the cost is shown in tokens only. Example entry: "gpt-example": {"input": 1.25, "cached_input": 0.125, "output": 10.0}. Optional key cache_write_input: the price of input tokens the provider writes to its prompt cache (the traces' cache_write_input_tokens, part of input); without it writes cost the input price, so a call costs what it did before writes were recorded. A write price above the input price makes every call with writes cost more, so --max-cost trips earlier; add it only as your account bills it. Optional key flex: the same four prices for calls the provider served on its Flex tier (the trace's service_tier); a call served on a tier without its own prices is billed at the standard ones, which undercounts a tier priced above standard (priority, which --llm-service-tier therefore does not offer). Optional key web_search_per_1k_calls: the web search tool's fee in US dollars per 1,000 calls, added to the tokens and never discounted by a tier. OpenAI's pricing page gives $10.00 / 1k calls without defining a call; cost.py bills each web_search_call item whose action is "search" (the tool guide: search actions incur the tool call cost), not the open_page and find_in_page items that read a page a search returned. Over the 18 uncached finding-runs of 2026-11-08 (two replicas of 9 findings) that is 3.56 / 3.22 searches per finding against 6.0 / 5.1 items, replica 1 / replica 2; if the billing dashboard shows the fee on every item, widen cost.BILLED_WEB_SEARCH_ACTIONS.
_gpt-6.1-sol: Checked on 2026-11-17 against developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (short context, up to 272K input tokens), the same table whose gpt-6.1-terra row matches the entry above: Standard 2.00 input, 0.10 cached input, 2.50 cache write, 10.00 output; Flex 1.00 / 0.05 / 1.25 / 5.00. Web search $10.00 / 1k calls. Used only to price the comparison's Codex Sol arm (run on a ChatGPT subscription, so nothing was billed); no Cognalys run uses this model.
_gpt-6.1-terra: Checked on 2026-11-09 against developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (short context, up to 272K input tokens): Standard 1.00 input, 0.05 cached input, 1.25 for the 30-minute cache write, 5.00 output; Flex 0.50 / 0.025 / 0.625 / 2.50. Web search $10.00 / 1k calls plus search content tokens at the model's rates.
_gpt-5.6-terra: The same page lists Standard 2.00 / 0.20 cached / 2.50 30-minute write / 12.00 and Flex 1.00 / 0.10 / 1.25 / 6.00. This entry keeps the prices the recorded gpt-5.6-terra runs (and the paper's cost figures) were computed with, 2.00 input and cached input and 12.00 output, until the account's bill confirms the page: no cache_write_input and no web_search_per_1k_calls, so cognalys cost reprices those runs as before rather than at a mix of the two price sets. Its Flex prices are half of these.
